arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Burns argued the state court's conclusion was unreasonable. She claimed it lacked viable support in the record.
Mr. DeSanctis argued the state court unreasonably denied a hearing. He claimed the court misjudged Brumfield's mental condition.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned the relevance of state evidence. He asked how state facts pertain to federal questions.
Justice Kennedy asked if state misinterpretation of federal rules creates violations. He probed the effect of low state standards.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Brumfield seeks a hearing on his intellectual disability claim. The state court denied this request. Brumfield argues the denial was unreasonable. The state argues its findings deserve federal deference.

paragraphs: Brumfield wants the Court to reject the state court's factual findings. He argues they were unreasonable under federal law.

paragraphs: Brumfield argues the state court's factual conclusion was unreasonable. He claims this violates federal habeas standards.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal review over state court fact-finding. It determines how strictly courts must examine state determinations of intellectual disability. The outcome shapes the balance between federal rights and state judicial authority.
